correctness.rationale: Invariance and self-adjointness reduce A and S into the same orthogonal blocks. After dividing by alpha, the Type-I extreme quotient is max(b+s,d)/min(a+s,c), s=1/alpha>0. If c<=a, the denominator stays c and a plateau at the limiting value exists exactly for 0<s<=d-b when d>b. If c>a, the quotient strictly decreases up to c-a: d/(a+s) decreases, and (b+s)/(a+s) also decreases unless b=a, in which case it is 1 and the former dominates to the breakpoint. To the right, the denominator is fixed, with the optimum attained exactly through max(c-a,d-b). Type II leaves one normalized block value 1 and the range [alpha c,alpha d] on the other block; equality with d/c is exactly inclusion of 1. These arguments include singleton spectra and all endpoint equalities. For A=diag(K,1), the condition numbers are K+1/alpha and, at alpha=1 for Type II, 1. Independent exact rational checks: 784 endpoint quadruples and 28,224 reciprocal parameter comparisons of both methods; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 2. The finite check does not replace the proof.
residual_risks: No extension to noninvariant reduced spaces or to Krylov iteration counts is established.

value.rationale: These are two existing algorithmic choices on a naturally spectral benchmark. The full classification answers when ridge tuning actually helps, identifies when its best value is only a limit, and supplies an unbounded quantitative separation from complement-only tuning even for a two-eigenvalue SPD system. The decision boundary and failure witness, not the routine spectral decomposition, give this narrow comparison its use.
residual_risks: This is an exact condition-number benchmark, not a claim about time to solution, robustness under loss of invariance or practical reduced solves.
